source.title: Token-level Data Selection for Safe LLM Fine-tuning
source.authors: Yan-Ping Li; Zhe-Ning Liu; Zijian Li; Zehong Lin; Jun Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates safety outcomes after fine-tuning on harmful-containing and benign datasets, and analyzes token-position distribution shifts. Its datasets, interventions, and measurements differ from the claim’s original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for harmful-containing and benign fine-tuning, as well as a token-position diagnosis. It does not test compliant-token prefilling, suffixes, decoding changes, safety localization in a small set of parameters, or training specifically to deepen safety. The references to those attacks and methods are background, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a defense paper, but it reports ASR for safety-aligned Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Llama-2-7B-Chat after standard LoRA SFT on a custom set mixing 22k harmful and 90k benign pairs (Table 17). That result bears on V1 in a new setting: mixed data, LoRA on q/k projections, keyword-matched ASR. The other results are the study's own defense against baselines, relative win rates against standard SFT, or a ΔKL diagnostic that differs from V3's construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that fine-tuning degrades safety and that the degrading signal is token-level: concentrated in initial response tokens but also scattered through the output, including in benign samples. They present TOSS and TOSS-Pro as token-level selection defenses that beat sample-level defenses on the safety–utility trade-off. The benign-data harm is asserted largely from cited work, not measured as an absolute change here.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates customization using LoRA fine-tuning on REDORCA and examines token-level diagnosis and data-selection defenses; its harmful data are mixed with utility data rather than tested as a small isolated fine-tuning set.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports varying outcomes with harmful-data proportion (30%, 50%, and 70%), model, token-discarding ratio, and the quality of the initial safety-degraded reference model.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning shifts the model's next-token distribution toward a harmful-tuned model mostly in the first few response tokens, but also significantly at mid and late positions (e.g. token 7). This is measured by ΔKL over custom-data tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning-induced safety drift is concentrated in early response tokens but not confined to them.

fits_no_version.finding: Masking the first five response tokens during fine-tuning gives a minor HEx-PHI safety gain over standard SFT but hurts SlimOrca utility (Figure 2 right, win rates).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Protecting only initial tokens during fine-tuning gives limited safety at a utility cost.

record.problems: The reported ASR values are post-fine-tuning outcomes without paired aligned-checkpoint ASR values in the cited table. The benign-data table reports win rates against standard SFT, not an aligned-model baseline. The token-position diagnosis is figure-based and uses a ΔKL different from V3’s specified aligned-versus-base KL. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded the additional harmfulness-score results in Appendix H, win-rate comparisons in Tables 1-2 and Table 20, utility metrics, and further fine-tuning/defense ablations because they are redundant or do not directly measure the named versions beyond the extracted ASR, benign safety win-rate, and token-position diagnosis. Excluded harmful-data-ratio utility outcomes from Table 6 because they do not measure safety behavior.

untested.parts: The few-to-few-hundred example scale. Only a 22k-harmful-in-112k mixed set is reported with ASR; the 500–1300-sample reference models have no ASR reported. No pre-fine-tuning ASR is given.
The benign fine-tuning experiment reports only win rates against standard SFT, with no absolute or pre/post harmful-compliance measure.
There is no aligned-versus-base per-token KL on harmful prompts. The ΔKL diagnostic is a different construct.
Not tested. TOSS is a data-filtering defense, not training that deepens safety.

missing.what: Standard SFT ASR and harmfulness in the OOD setting, with privacy-category harmful data added: ASR about 94.68 and 87.57, harmfulness 3.01 and 4.17.

record.verdict_notes: Table 17 values for Llama-3 were shifted in three rows: R3 should be 86.96, R4 93.28, and R6 92.96. Most rows are defense comparisons or relative win rates and are unlinked. Neither original source (2310.03693, 2406.05946) is this study.

versions.untested_parts: The custom fine-tuning dataset includes 22k harmful pairs mixed with 90k SLIMORCA pairs; the paper does not test isolated fine-tuning with only a few to a few hundred harmful examples. Its ASR table reports post-fine-tuning outcomes, not a paired pre-fine-tuning aligned-model ASR.
The benign-data experiment reports safety win rates relative to standard SFT, not a direct comparison of harmful compliance before and after benign fine-tuning on an aligned checkpoint.

The paper measures ΔKL between the customized model’s divergence from a safe base and from a safety-degraded model on custom-dataset response tokens. This is not a direct aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement on harmful prompts.

rows.subject: customized model (base model not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Measured per-token ΔKL between the customized model’s divergence from the safe base and from the safety-degraded model.
rows.note: Text says the most pronounced shifts toward the safety-degraded model occur in the initial few generated tokens, but significant divergence also occurs at middle and later positions, including token 7. This is not the exact KL measurement specified by V3.
rows.check: ΔKL compares the fine-tuned model's divergence from the safe base with its divergence from a harmful-tuned model, over custom-data tokens. That is not V3's aligned-versus-base KL on harmful prompts. The result is figure-only. Moved to fits_no_version.

relationships.condition: Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Llama-2-7B-Chat, standard LoRA SFT on REDORCA (22k harmful + 90k benign pairs), keyword-matched ASR on ANTHROPIC HH and HEx-PHI
relationships.reason: Post-fine-tuning ASR is 86.96–96.25% (R2, R3, R16, R17), and the authors state safety is significantly degraded. No pre-fine-tuning ASR is reported, and the harmful set is far larger than V1's few hundred.
relationships.display_finding: Post-fine-tuning attack success was 86.96–96.25% and the authors state safety was significantly degraded, but no pre-fine-tuning rate is given and the harmful set is far larger than a few hundred examples.

relation.reason: Reports absolute ASR after standard fine-tuning and diagnoses safety degradation, beyond comparing defense methods.

tranche.reason: Reports harmful compliance after LoRA customization on mixed harmful and benign REDORCA data, providing a result in a new setting.

source_check.notes: No paired pre-fine-tuning ASR is reported; degradation relies partly on the authors' interpretation. Keyword-matched ASR after 22k harmful pairs does not independently establish V1's stated low dose.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Standard SFT on REDORCA with harmful and benign examples, evaluated on ANTHROPIC HH and HEx-PHI
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports high post-fine-tuning ASR values for both models under standard SFT (R2, R3, R16, R17), while noting that standard SFT degrades safety. The tested custom dataset is much larger and mixed, not a few-to-hundreds-only harmful set.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Benign custom dataset; safety win rates relative to standard SFT
reader_labels.reason: The benign-data experiment measures safety benchmark outcomes, but its comparison is standard SFT rather than the aligned pre-fine-tuning model, so it does not establish the claimed increase in harmful compliance from benign fine-tuning (R30-R35).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Token positions in responses from the custom dataset
reader_labels.reason: The reported ΔKL shift is most pronounced in the initial few tokens, but the paper also reports significant mid- and later-position divergence, including token 7; its measure is not the direct aligned-versus-base KL specified by the claim (R1).
